record.paper_title: ANSWERING TWO OPEN PROBLEMS ON BANKS THEOREM FOR NON-AUTONOMOUS DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS
record.context_brief: Counterexample to the non-finitely-generated Banks-type extension
record.original_question: Does there exist a non-autonomous dynamical system (X, f1,∞) on a metric space X without isolated points such that f1,∞ is topologically transitive, every point of X is periodic for the system, there exist two invariant periodic points x and y whose orbits orb(x, f1,∞) and orb(y, f1,∞) are disjoint, the system is not finitely generated (so the set of maps occurring in the sequence f1, f2, ... is infinite), and yet the system is not sensitive in the sense that there is no ε > 0 with the property that every neighborhood contains a point whose orbit eventually separates by at least ε from the original orbit?

evidence.quote: Theorem 4. [8, Theorem 3.1] Let X be a metric space without isolate points. Suppose that a finitely generated NADS (X, f1,∞) satisfies the following conditions: (1) f1,∞ is topologically transitive; (2) Per(f1,∞) = X; (3) there exist two invariant periodic points x, y ∈ X such that orb(x, f1,∞) ∩ orb(y, f1,∞) = ∅. Then, (X, f1,∞) is sensitive.
Open Problem 5. [8, Open Problem 4.1] Is there any counterexample of a NADS, which is not finitely generated but satisfies other conditions of Theorem 4, fails to be sensitive?
Remark 8. Example 7 shows that there exists a NADS, which is not finitely generated but satisfies other conditions of Theorem 4, fails to be sensitive, giving a positive answer to Open Problem 5.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved positively: an explicit counterexample was constructed showing that without the finitely-generated hypothesis, the conditions of Banks-type theorem (transitivity, dense periodic points, two disjoint invariant periodic orbits) do not imply sensitivity. The construction appears in the zbMATH-indexed work titled "Answering two open problems on Banks theorem for non-autonomous dynamical systems."
